title: Exhaustive transfinite filtration by invariant coordinate submodules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a set and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of $R$-modules. Put $M=\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], and let $M_A\subseteq M$ denote the families supported in $A\subseteq J$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule]. Let $f:M\to M$ be $R$-linear. Suppose that for every $j\in J$ a specified at most countable subset $D_j\subseteq J$ contains $j$ and satisfies $f(M_{D_j})\subseteq M_{D_j}$. Then there exist a set ordinal $\kappa$, a bijective enumeration $\eta:\{\beta:\beta<\kappa\}\to J$, and an increasing family $(A_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$ of subsets of $J$ with the following properties. One has $A_0=\varnothing$, $A_\kappa=J$, and $A_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}A_\beta$ at every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\kappa$. For $\alpha<\kappa$, if $A_\alpha=J$ then $A_{\alpha+1}=A_\alpha$; otherwise, for the least $\gamma<\kappa$ with $\eta(\gamma)\notin A_\alpha$, one has $A_{\alpha+1}=A_\alpha\cup D_{\eta(\gamma)}$. Every difference $A_{\alpha+1}\setminus A_\alpha$ is at most countable, and $\eta(\{\beta:\beta<\alpha\})\subseteq A_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\leq\kappa$. The coordinate submodules satisfy $M_{A_0}=0$, $M_{A_\kappa}=M$, $f(M_{A_\alpha})\subseteq M_{A_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha\leq\kappa$, and $M_{A_\lambda}=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}M_{A_\beta}$ at every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\kappa$. No countable-generation assumption on the $N_j$ is required.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem] choose a well-order on $J$. Apply [lem-trf-well-order-ordinal-enumeration] to obtain a set ordinal $\kappa$ and a bijection $\eta:\{\beta<\kappa\}\to J$ in that order. This includes $J=\varnothing$, when $\kappa=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] on the set of ordinals $\alpha\leq\kappa$, with values in $\mathcal P(J)$. Put $A_0=\varnothing$; at a nonzero limit put $A_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}A_\beta$; at a successor keep $A_\alpha$ if it is $J$, and otherwise put $A_{\alpha+1}=A_\alpha\cup D_{\eta(\gamma)}$, where $\gamma$ is the least index with $\eta(\gamma)\notin A_\alpha$. Such an index exists by surjectivity of $\eta$, and has a least value in the ordinal order. The rule depends only on earlier values. Transfinite induction proves $A_\beta\subseteq A_\alpha$ for $\beta<\alpha$: successors contain the preceding set, and a limit contains each preceding set by its union formula.

proof.text: From [def-trf-coordinate-submodule], $B\subseteq C$ implies $M_B\subseteq M_C$, and $M_{B\cup C}=M_B+M_C$: split a finite-support family into its coordinates in $B$ and its remaining coordinates in $C\setminus B$. These restrictions have finite support by [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Thus if $f$ preserves $M_B$ and $M_C$, linearity gives $f(x_B+x_C)=f(x_B)+f(x_C)\in M_{B\cup C}$. At stage zero $M_\varnothing=0$ is invariant. At each successor the induction hypothesis and the assumed invariance of the selected $M_{D_{\eta(\gamma)}}$ give invariance of $M_{A_{\alpha+1}}$; a stationary stage needs no change.

source.place: Tag 058X (theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum), proof: coordinate transfinite recursion, lines 20500–20533, and exhaustion, lines 20555–20565; specified invariant blocks replace the countable-matrix construction.

proof.text: Let $0<\lambda\leq\kappa$ be a limit. For $x\in M_{A_\lambda}$ its finite support $F$ lies in $\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}A_\beta$ by [def-trf-coordinate-submodule] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. For each $j\in F$ choose $\beta_j<\lambda$ with $j\in A_{\beta_j}$. If $F$ is nonempty its finitely many indices have a maximum $\delta<\lambda$, so monotonicity gives $F\subseteq A_\delta$; if $F$ is empty take $\delta=0<\lambda$. Therefore $x\in M_{A_\delta}$. The reverse inclusion is monotonicity, giving $M_{A_\lambda}=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}M_{A_\beta}$. If earlier stages are invariant, then $f(x)\in M_{A_\delta}\subseteq M_{A_\lambda}$. Together with the preceding step, transfinite induction proves invariance at every stage.

source.place: Tag 058X (theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum), proof: coordinate transfinite recursion, lines 20500–20533, and exhaustion, lines 20555–20565; specified invariant blocks replace the countable-matrix construction.

proof.text: Transfinite induction proves $\eta(\{\beta<\alpha\})\subseteq A_\alpha$. The assertion is empty at zero. At $\alpha+1$ earlier elements persist; if $\eta(\alpha)$ is missing from $A_\alpha$, all indices below $\alpha$ are already present by induction, so the least missing index is exactly $\alpha$. Since $\eta(\alpha)\in D_{\eta(\alpha)}$, the successor adds it. If it was already present nothing is needed. At a nonzero limit $\lambda$, each $\beta<\lambda$ has $\beta+1<\lambda$, so $\eta(\beta)\in A_{\beta+1}\subseteq A_\lambda$. Surjectivity of $\eta$ now gives $A_\kappa=J$, without any assumption that the individual $N_j$ are nonzero.

source.place: Tag 058X (theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum), proof: coordinate transfinite recursion, lines 20500–20533, and exhaustion, lines 20555–20565; specified invariant blocks replace the countable-matrix construction.

proof.text: At a nonstationary successor, $A_{\alpha+1}\setminus A_\alpha\subseteq D_{\eta(\gamma)}$, so the difference is at most countable by restricting a countability injection for that specified block; at a stationary successor the difference is empty. By [def-trf-coordinate-submodule], families supported in $\varnothing$ are zero and every family is supported in $J$, hence $M_{A_0}=0$ and $M_{A_\kappa}=M$. All other requested identities are the recursion and the preceding steps. Only finite support and the hypotheses on the specified $D_j$ were used, so no generation assumption on $N_j$ enters.
